title: Block: Build a String
oneLiner: Interleave two strings character by character, then append whatever is left of the longer one.
keyTakeaway: Build strings from pieces and join once: StringBuilder in C#, a list and "".join in Python. Adding to a string in a loop copies it every time.
explanation:
Return a string that takes one character from a, then one from b, and so on; when one runs out, the rest of the other follows. ("abc", "12") gives "a1b2c".

Loop i from 0 to the longer length, appending a[i] if i is inside a and b[i] if i is inside b. Collect into a StringBuilder (C#) or a list of characters (Python) and turn it into a string once at the end. Strings are immutable in both languages, so s += c in a loop builds a new string each time: O(n²) for long inputs.

gotchas: Adding to a string inside the loop, which copies the whole string on every append.

complexity.note: Each character of both strings is appended once and the result is joined once.
